value.rationale: Second-order cones are canonical constraint sets. The theorem identifies precisely when a naturally defined nearest-point map can be used without expanding perturbations in the ambient non-Hilbert geometry, for every real exponent, slope and finite dimension. The exact, sharp planar stability invariant has a structurally exceptional aperture \(\kappa=1\) that disappears upon adding a second transverse coordinate. The dimension transition and global parameter classification answer an intrinsic robustness question rather than tabulating arbitrary numerical cases.
